Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee
 Order

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seek quashing of FIR No.0694/2022 dated 31.12.2022 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Ambedkar Nagar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 12.07.2022 arrived at between the parties before the Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi.
2.

This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 12.07.2022 [Annexure-P-2] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners W.P.(CRL) 3724/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/12/2023 at 01:14:35 and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 4 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned ASC accepts notice.
She confirms that since the FIR involves matrimonial disputes, she has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 28.08.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement dated 12.07.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD no.520542 issued on 15.12.2023 [ICICI Bank]in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present,
past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr. (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
